matches.reasoning: Real Madrid, despite its own injury concerns in the paint (Tavares, Len, Garuba out), faces a Tenerife side severely depleted by injuries to key players like Shermadini, Fitipaldo, and Giedraitis (all out), and Huertas (doubtful/injured). Real Madrid is the stronger team historically and in the regular season, playing at home in a crucial Game 3, coming off a dominant 118-83 away win in Game 2 against Tenerife.
key_factors: Severe injury crisis for Tenerife, sidelining multiple key starters and leaders (Shermadini, Fitipaldo, Giedraitis out; Huertas doubtful/injured).
Real Madrid plays at home in Game 3 of the playoffs, which offers a significant advantage.
Real Madrid won Game 2 convincingly (118-83) away from home, indicating good form despite earlier struggles.
Real Madrid was the top seed in the regular season (25-7/26-8 record), demonstrating overall superiority.
matches.injury_notes: Real Madrid is without key big men Edy Tavares, Alex Len, and Usman Garuba, but has brought in reinforcements Ömer Yurtseven and Mady Sissoko. Tenerife is severely hit: Rokas Giedraitis (ACL tear, out for season), Giorgi Shermadini (cardiac arrhythmia, out for weeks), Bruno Fitipaldo (calf injury, out for 6 weeks, season over), Marcelinho Huertas (hamstring tear, doubtful/injured), and Aaron Doornekamp (quadriceps overload, doubtful). They have signed Elvar Fridriksson and Kevin Yebo as replacements.
